7. He also submits that for an effective service of notice under section 138(1A)(b) of the Act there has to be an acknowledgement due, which is absent in the present case. Further, as per the averments of the complainant his legal notice was returned unserved on 30-9-2013 and 6-10-2013 respectively with the remarks –“প্রাপক বর্তমানে দেশের বাইরে এবং প্রাপক সর্বদা অনুপস্থিত থাকায় ফেরত দেয়া হইল”. As such, he submits that the complainant was not at all required to wait till completion of 30 (thirty) days, as has been prescribed under section 138(1) clause (c), rather his cause of action to file the case having arisen on 6-10-2013 hence, filing the petition of complaint on 24-11-2013 is barred by limitation. 

 18. The other contention of the accused petitioner is that the cause of action having arisen on 6-10-2013 since the legal notice was returned unserved for being absent in his last known address hence, the option to file the case within 30 (thirty) days from 6-10-2013 is redundant. Said contention of the petitioner is again a misconceived proposition, for, Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881 is a special law and the period of limitation as prescribed in section 138 has mandatory effect which starts from the date of presenting the cheque. Since vide section 138(1)(c) of the Act the legislature has given 30 (thirty) days’ time to the drawer to make necessary arrangement for making payment but having not complied with the said requirement the case cannot be dislodged on the plea that the cause of action to file the case arose on 6-10-2013 for the notice was returned on 6-10-2013 with the remarks “প্রাপক বর্তমানে দেশের বাইরে এবং প্রাপক সর্বদা অনুপস্থিত থাকায় ফেরত দেয়া হইল”
